verdict.rationale: CodeRabbit documents a Learnings knowledge base: review preferences taught through natural-language chat are stored and applied automatically to future reviews, learnings are retained as code-related data, and it auto-detects convention files such as CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md as review criteria. However, the evidence only shows learning from explicit chat instruction, not a memory built from past review decisions themselves (accepted or dismissed comments, resolved threads), and the only community comment hedges that it 'supposedly' remembers. Missing for 10: documented capture of past review decisions beyond chat-taught preferences, detail on how learnings are scoped, viewed, edited and applied across repos, and independent hands-on corroboration that learnings measurably change future PR reviews.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the reviewer builds a persistent memory of my team's conventions and past review decisions and applies it to future PRs

citations.quote: Review preferences CodeRabbit learns from your chat conversations and applies automatically to future reviews.
Teach CodeRabbit your review preferences using natural-language chat.
Data retention only affects storage of code-related data such as learnings and review context
CodeRabbit automatically detects coding guideline files such as .cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, and AGENTS.md in your repository and applies them as review criteria
